verdict.rationale: Chroma offers copy-on-write collection forking for dataset versioning and A/B testing, which gives an isolated copy to test against while original data stays shared and unchanged. Its CLI can also run a local server, separate from Cloud production DBs. These are Chroma's own features, but the docs never frame them as a sandbox or test environment, and they do not explicitly state that writes to a fork cannot affect the source. missing for 10: explicit sandbox/staging environment documentation, documented isolation guarantees for fork writes versus production, hands-on corroboration of safe testing workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Dataset versioning, A/B testing, and roll-outs
Forks are copy-on-write. You only pay for incremental storage written after the fork; unchanged data remains shared.
The Chroma CLI lets you run a Chroma server locally on your machine
